items.prompt: What do the elbowed antennae on an ant help identify about it?

options.label: That it is a wasp
options.feedback: Ants evolved from wasps, but the elbowed antennae are a feature that marks a creature as an ant, not as a wasp today.

options.label: That it is a bee
options.feedback: Bees are related to ants, but they do not have elbowed antennae; that bend is an ant's own recognizable trait.

options.label: That it is an ant
options.feedback: Yes, the geniculate, or elbowed, antennae are one of the clear signs that an insect is an ant.

options.label: That it is a termite
options.feedback: Termites have straight, beaded antennae, not elbowed ones; the bent antennae point to an ant, not a termite.

items.ko_line: Elbowed antennae are a giveaway for ants.
items.exp_text: An ant's antennae have a distinct elbow-like bend, which is one of the main ways to tell an ant from other insects. This is a simple physical trait, not something the ant does.

items.prompt: Which of these is a caste found in a typical ant colony?

options.label: Nymphs
options.feedback: Nymphs are young of insects that do not undergo complete metamorphosis, but ants have a different life cycle with larvae and pupae, so this is not a caste here.

options.label: Workers
options.feedback: Correct, most ants in a colony are sterile wingless females that work, and these are called workers.

options.label: Drones that lay eggs
options.feedback: Drones are fertile males, and they do not lay eggs; that task belongs to the queen, so this label mixes up roles.

options.label: Queens that forage
options.feedback: Queens are fertile females whose main job is reproduction, not foraging; foraging is done by workers.

items.ko_line: Workers form the bulk of a colony.
items.exp_text: A typical ant colony has sterile wingless females as workers, plus soldiers, fertile males called drones, and one or more queens. Workers are the ones that do most of the daily tasks.

items.prompt: How are the workers in an ant colony best described?

options.label: They are fertile females that lay eggs
options.feedback: It is the queen that is the fertile female laying eggs; workers are sterile, so they cannot lay eggs.

options.label: They are males that mate with the queen
options.feedback: Males are called drones, and they are a separate caste from workers; workers are always sterile females.

options.label: They are wingless males that defend the nest
options.feedback: Defenders are soldiers, and workers are not males; they are sterile wingless females.

options.label: They are sterile, wingless females
options.feedback: Yes, typical workers are sterile, wingless females that do the colony's work.

items.ko_line: Workers are the sterile female caste.
items.exp_text: In most ant colonies, the workers are sterile wingless females. They form the majority and handle tasks like foraging and nest care, while the queen is the one that reproduces.

items.prompt: What is the main job of the queen ant in a colony?

options.label: To lay eggs
options.feedback: Correct, the queen ant is the fertile female whose primary role is to produce eggs for the colony.

options.label: To find food for the nest
options.feedback: Foraging for food is the work of the workers, not the queen.

options.label: To fight off invaders
options.feedback: Defending the colony is usually the task of soldier ants, not the queen.

options.label: To build the nest walls
options.feedback: Nest construction is done by workers; the queen's focus is reproduction.

items.ko_line: The queen is the egg layer.
items.exp_text: In an ant colony, the queen's main job is to lay eggs, providing new individuals for the colony. She does not forage, build, or fight.

items.prompt: On which continent are there no native ants?

options.label: Australia
options.feedback: Australia has many native ant species; it is not the continent lacking them.

options.label: South America
options.feedback: South America has a rich ant fauna, so it is not the right answer.

options.label: Antarctica
options.feedback: Correct, Antarctica is the only continent with no indigenous ants.

options.label: Africa
options.feedback: Africa is home to countless ant species, so it is not the one without ants.

items.ko_line: Antarctica is the only continent without ants.
items.exp_text: Ants are found on every continent except Antarctica. They have colonized almost all landmasses, but the frozen continent remains free of them.

items.prompt: What is the term for a colony so unified that it acts like a single organism?

options.label: A caste system
options.feedback: A caste system describes the different roles inside a colony, but it does not capture the idea of the whole colony acting as one unit.

options.label: A superorganism
options.feedback: Yes, ant colonies are called superorganisms because the ants work together as if they were one entity.

options.label: A society
options.feedback: Ant societies do have division of labor, but the specific term for the single-unity behavior is superorganism.

options.label: A hive
options.feedback: Hive is a word for a bee's nest structure, not the term for ant colony unity.

items.ko_line: A superorganism is the whole colony acting as one.
items.exp_text: Ant colonies are described as superorganisms because the ants appear to operate as a unified entity, working together for the colony's good rather than as many separate individuals.

items.prompt: What do termites share with ants that makes them be called 'white ants'?

options.label: They have the same body shape with a narrow waist
options.feedback: Termites do not have the narrow waist that ants have; their bodies are broader, so this is not a shared trait.

options.label: They have elbowed antennae
options.feedback: Termites have straight, beaded antennae, not the elbowed kind found on ants.

options.label: They belong to the same insect order
options.feedback: Ants are in the order Hymenoptera, while termites are in the order Blattodea, so they are in different orders.

options.label: They live in colonies with sterile workers
options.feedback: Yes, both ants and termites are eusocial, having sterile workers that care for the nest, which is why termites are sometimes called 'white ants'.

items.exp_text: Termites are called 'white ants' because they, like ants, live in colonies with sterile workers. But termites are only distantly related to ants, being in the cockroach order instead.

items.prompt: What sort of food do most ant species eat?

options.label: A wide variety of both plants and animals
options.feedback: Correct, most ant species are omnivorous generalists, eating many different kinds of food.

options.label: Only nectar from flowers
options.feedback: Nectar is a food for some, but most ants are not limited to nectar; they eat much more.

options.label: Only other insects
options.feedback: While some ants are predators, most are not specialists that eat only insects.

options.label: Only leaves and wood
options.feedback: Leaves and wood are eaten by certain specialists, but most ants are not limited to these plant materials.

items.exp_text: Most ant species are omnivorous generalists, meaning they eat a wide range of foods including plant matter and other animals. A few species are specialists, but they are the exception.
